name: X-Cart
title: X-Cart SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on X-Cart 5.5.1+: 26 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; vendors are the gap. Setup, API key, environment and fixes.
lede: Solid core coverage: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against X-Cart’s modern API, and the one recorded gap is vendors. Every call carries the store’s API key; a shopper’s token joins it after sign-in.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; vendors are the one recorded gap. Cart and checkout need X-Cart’s read/write API key, and the connector takes it from a `PUBLIC_` variable, which the browser receives.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your X-Cart store

env.name: PUBLIC_X_CART_API_URL
env.note: Your X-Cart store’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_X_CART_API_KEY
env.note: The store API key from X-Cart’s Settings › API, sent as `X-Auth-Token` on every call. A read-only key rejects writes, so cart and checkout need the read/write key. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_X_CART_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: Sent as a bearer token when set; a shopper’s token after sign-in travels the same way.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/x-cart-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_X_CART_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_X_CART_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_X_CART_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_X_CART_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_X_CART_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Run X-Cart 5.5.1 or later. The connector follows the modern API; the `_key` query parameter of the 5.3/5.4 admin API does not exist there and is not used.
Create the API key under Settings › API — the read/write one, because a read-only key rejects every cart and checkout write.
howItWorks: X-Cart 5.5.1 and later want two headers: `X-Auth-Token`, the store API key, on every call, and `Authorization: Bearer`, the shopper’s token, once they have signed in. A read-only key is enough to browse but rejects every POST, PATCH and DELETE.
limitations: The store API key, sent as `X-Auth-Token`, comes from `PUBLIC_X_CART_API_KEY` — and cart and checkout need the read/write key. SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser, so every visitor to the store can read it.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the x-cart connector is active but PUBLIC_X_CART_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_X_CART_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

faq.q: Can I run an X-Cart store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, and vendors are the only recorded gap. The obstacle is the key: cart and checkout need X-Cart’s read/write API key, which the connector reads from a `PUBLIC_` variable that every visitor’s browser receives.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to X-Cart?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/x-cart-connector`, set `PUBLIC_X_CART_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Which X-Cart versions and keys does the connector need?
faq.a: X-Cart 5.5.1 or later, and the read/write store API key from Settings › API, sent as `X-Auth-Token`. A read-only key can browse but rejects cart and checkout writes.

api.surface: The connector calls X-Cart’s Storefront API, a REST API in Hydra JSON-LD under `/api/storefront`, and reaches the admin API under `/api` only to read the signed-in customer’s orders.
api.auth: Every call carries the store API key as `X-Auth-Token`; a shopper signs in with `POST /api/storefront/auth/login`, whose JWT goes out as `Authorization: Bearer`, and on a 401 the connector tries `POST /auth/refresh` once, which works only when a refresh token was captured, because the login response returns the refresh token as a server cookie.

calls.what: `GET /api/storefront/products/compact` with `page`, `itemsPerPage`, `filter.substring`, `filter.categories`, `filter.bestsellers` and `order_by.<field>`; a product page uses `GET /products/detailed/by_clean_url/{clean_url}` or `GET /products/detailed/{id}`

`POST /api/storefront/carts` creates the cart; then `GET /carts/{uuid}`, `POST /carts/{uuid}/items`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /carts/{uuid}/items/{id}`, `POST /carts/{uuid}/coupons` and `POST /carts/{uuid}/calculate`
`GET /api/orders` on the admin API with `profile.login` set to the e-mail from `GET /api/storefront/auth/whoami`
`GET`, `POST`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/api/storefront/users/self/addresses`, with the field list from `GET /address_fields`
`GET /api/storefront/carts/{uuid}/payment_methods`; X-Cart has no store-wide payment-method list

rules: Requests send `Accept: application/ld+json` because only that type returns collections in the Hydra envelope with `hydra:totalItems`, and with `application/json` X-Cart answers with a bare array and no total.
Filters and sorting are flat parameters, `filter.<field>` and `order_by.<field>=asc|desc`, and products sort only by name, price, `arrivalDate` and sales, so any other sort is left off.

The cart is a UUID returned by `POST /carts` and replayed in every `/carts/{uuid}/...` path; the connector keeps it in an `xc-cart` cookie, the name X-Cart’s own storefront uses, and on sign-in merges the anonymous cart into the account with `POST /carts/{uuid}/merge`.

The admin `/api/orders` collection covers every customer, so the connector always sends `profile.login` with the signed-in shopper’s e-mail, then drops any returned row whose e-mail does not match, in case the store ignores the filter.

Payment runs on the cart’s payment transaction with `PATCH /carts/{uuid}/payment/{id}`, and when `action: init` returns a hosted-gateway URL the connector sends the shopper there and places no order until they return.
